text:
anja: Heads-up — after yesterday's runtime push I'm seeing a reproducible p99 spike on KV-heavy long-context workloads. med ~28ms, p99 up to ~420ms on some hosts. Happens under sustained batch merges (long seqs + batch size 12-16).

mike: Was that the FIFO eviction roll we flipped last week? Any repro steps?

anja: Yes FIFO went live in canary. Quick repro: run the long-context perf canary (seq=8192, batch=16, kv_per_req~450) for ~5m. Saw a persistent latency tail right after warmup.

devon: Interesting — on a quick flamegraph the hotspot looks like `kv::reinsert_locked` and a ton of time in list manipulation + mutex contention. Seems reinserts during eviction are expensive with our FIFO path.

lisa: I ran a synthetic run: before flip (LRU) p99 ~65ms, after flip (FIFO) p99 ~410ms under the same load. Mem usage similar, but major uptick in minor page faults and scheduler stalls.

jordan: I captured `perf top` and `perf record` traces — page-faults jumped ~3x, and we see syscalls to `mremap`/`munmap` coming from our paging layer when eviction churn is high. Kernel shows increased kswapd activity on the node.

anja: Paste of the flame snippet:
```
flamegraph: kv::reinsert_locked 45%
           eviction_list::splice 18%
           std::mutex::lock 12%
           scheduler::park 9%
```
Not exact symbols but clear hotspot around reinserts + list ops.

mike: Do we have a correctness issue too or only perf? Could FIFO be causing repeated reinserts of the same node while another thread is iterating the list, invalidating iterators and making the evict loop O(n^2)?

devon: That's my read — we do a remove+push_back on hits. Under concurrency a node can be reinserted multiple times in a single eviction sweep, causing the eviction loop to keep seeing recently-touched nodes and spin. LRU had a cheaper path where we only bump timestamps and do lazy promotion, so less list churn.

lisa: Repro parameters I used:
- seq_len: 8192
- batch: 16
- kv per request: 450+-50
- run duration: 10m
Observed: p50 ~30ms, p95 ~110ms, p99 ~410ms. Swap-in count + page-faults correlated with tail spikes.

anja: Immediate mitigation: flip back to LRU for the canary pool and throttle batch merges. You can toggle via runtime config API:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/runtime-config -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"kv_eviction_policy":"lru","batch_merge_max":12}'
```
I'll schedule an emergency rollback if we see more infra-wide impact. :rotating_light:

deploy-bot: rollback started for canary group `canary-usa-west-2` (deploy id dpl_2024_09_21_18)

mike: Any data-loss or correctness regressions observed while FIFO was active?

anja: No correctness errors observed (no dropped tokens, no corrupted cache entries). But there's a race where if reinserts interleave with eviction iterators it can lead to temporarily skipping recently-used nodes and evicting active segments — this is a correctness risk under heavier concurrency. We didn't hit silent corruption, but it's risky.

devon: Proposed immediate patch (small): avoid physical reinserts on hit inside the eviction sweep path. Instead, set a `touched` bit and defer list mutation to a dedicated async worker that batches reinserts. Pseudocode:
```cpp
if (evicting) { node->touched = true; } else if (!in_list(node)) { push_back(node); }
// async worker: scan touched bits and move nodes to tail in bulk under a single lock
```
This should limit list churn and reduce mutex contention.

lisa: Agreed. Also add a unit test that simulates concurrent hits+evict sweep and asserts no iterator invalidation. I'll file test + perf harness.

mike: Sounds good. Please include metrics: p50/p95/p99 and minor page-fault rate before/after in the PR so we can evaluate.

anja: I'll open the PR with the deferred reinserts + perf numbers and attach the raw flamegraphs. Targeting hotfix release today after review.

jordan: Also worth exploring a soft watermark to start paging earlier (reduce peak KV entries) and throttle batch merges when eviction queue depth > threshold. That buys us headroom until the reinserts patch lands.

anja: Thanks — will coordinate the throttle + revert on canary. Updating the incident doc in #incidents with links to traces.

lisa: I'll write the short postmortem + mitigation steps once PR merges.

mike: Thanks team. Good catch on the FIFO reinsertion pattern — lesson: cheaper eviction policy can still be worse under concurrency. :thumbsup:
